result:
I audited the repo against the live site and the GSC export. Here's what's going on:

**The core issue: this SaaS pivoted products, and the SEO footprint didn't follow.** The brand used to be "InboxZap" (email cleanup tool) and is now "Lumina" (AI meeting-notes assistant) — totally different product, totally different audience. But:

- All 12 blog posts (and nearly all GSC impressions — thousands each) are still 100% old InboxZap content: "Gmail Storage Full?", "Bulk Delete Emails", "Unsubscribe From Newsletters," etc. None of this is relevant to a meeting-assistant buyer, which is almost certainly why rankings have crumbled to position 40-60 despite high impressions — zero clicks, zero conversions even when it does show up.
- `app/layout.tsx` still exports site-wide `<title>`/description/OG tags branded "InboxZap — Clean Your Inbox in Minutes," while actual page content (and the live site's homepage) is Lumina. That's a real, concrete bug — wrong brand in search results/social previews on every page.
- The blog index (`/blog`) renders nothing server-side — it `fetch()`s `/api/posts`, which doesn't exist (404), so crawlers see an empty "Loading posts…" shell with no links to the posts.
- `sitemap.ts` has a literal `// TODO: include blog posts` and only lists 4 static URLs.
- `/features` and `/pricing` work on the live site with good Lumina content, but there's no source for them in this repo at all (404 if you actually build this repo) — so the repo is behind production.
- Nav/footer link to `/faq`; it redirects to `/#faq`, but the homepage has no FAQ section — dead end, and a missed opportunity (FAQ content is good for long-tail queries + featured snippets).

**The one strategic call I want to flag before I touch content:** what to do with those 12 legacy blog posts. My take — redirect them (301) rather than try to rewrite them, since "bulk delete emails" and "meeting notes" have no real audience overlap, and keeping zombie off-topic content actively hurts the site's topical relevance for what it's selling now. The alternative is rewriting a couple where there's a plausible bridge (e.g., "email overload" → "meeting overload"), but that's weaker content than writing fresh posts aimed at actual Lumina buyers.

Want me to proceed with: (1) fix the layout metadata bug, (2) rebuild `/features`, `/pricing`, `/faq` as real pages, (3) fix the blog to be server-rendered with a real sitemap, and (4) 301-redirect the legacy posts and write new posts targeting actual Lumina keywords (AI meeting notes, meeting transcription, auto-generated action items, etc.)? Or would you rather keep/rewrite some of the legacy posts instead of redirecting them?
